correctness.rationale: Cauchy–Binet gives the sum of three squared minors including a zero minor for coincident times, so independent replicates yield equal objective values at the endpoints. The reduced objective has derivative with the sign pattern of an affine sinusoid of period π: its amplitude strictly exceeds the offset by the squared-amplitude test, since sinh(ηΦ)>η|sin Φ|. The endpoint derivative signs force only a minimum in the short interval; at Φ=θ the terminal zero crosses downward, so it is positive immediately to the left and there is still no interior maximum. For θ<Φ<π the negative terminal derivative beats both equal endpoints; there is at most one interior downward crossing. For Φ≥π the multiplicative decay per π excludes every later period from positive global optimality, and the test x=θ strictly beats the endpoints of [0,π], including resonances. For Φ=π (and all integral multiples) factoring the sin² gives x=θ directly. Uniform convergence to the limiting objective and F₀′(θ)=−2 then give an O(q) root displacement; Taylor expansion and the uniformly bounded phase derivative of the perturbation give the stated first-order term and O(q²) remainder. Fixing small positive and negative residual phases makes that leading sign alternate on unbounded sequences. An independent direct Gram-matrix calculation spot-checked the reported two interior examples and a multiple-period resonance.
residual_risks: Nonmaterial proof typo at line 98: f(π)≤f(0), not always strict; equality occurs when sin Φ=0. The strict dominance f(θ)>f(0) in (9) already supplies the needed conclusion in both cases.
The expansion is for fixed positive η; the finite diagnostic does not certify all horizons.

value.rationale: The exact threshold resolves whether to spend a third real measurement on replication or on a new sample, and the first-period conclusion avoids a global search over an arbitrary number of periods. The sign of the long-horizon bias is a substantive distinction from monotonically approaching an optimal placement. These conclusions are naturally tied to the information design and not fine-tuned examples.
